recipes.title: Lentil, Spinach & Tomato Stew
recipes.intro: A thick, warming lentil stew that keeps well and reheats easily.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Lentils and spinach are two of the foods Moon Cycle features for iron in the Menstrual phase, and lemon adds vitamin C, which helps with absorbing plant iron.
steps: Soften the chopped onion and carrots in the oil for 5 minutes, then stir in the garlic and cumin for 1 minute.
Add the lentils, tomatoes and stock. Bring to the boil, then simmer for 25 minutes until the lentils are tender.
Stir in the spinach and let it wilt for 2 minutes.
Squeeze in the lemon juice, season to taste and serve hot.

recipes.title: Beef & Kidney Bean Chilli
recipes.intro: A mild, family-style chilli that is better the next day. Serve with rice or bread.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Beef and kidney beans are featured Menstrual foods for iron, and the peppers and tomatoes add vitamin C.
steps: Brown the mince in the oil in a large pan for 6 minutes, breaking it up.
Add the chopped onion and pepper and cook for 5 minutes, then the garlic, cumin and chilli powder.
Pour in the tomatoes and the drained beans, with a splash of water.
Simmer for 15 minutes until thick, season and serve.

recipes.title: Black Bean, Quinoa & Orange Bowl
recipes.intro: A colourful bowl that works warm or cold and packs well for lunch.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Black beans and quinoa are featured Menstrual foods for plant-based iron, while the orange and pepper add vitamin C to the same bowl.
steps: Rinse the quinoa and simmer in twice its volume of water for 15 minutes, then drain and fluff.
Warm the drained beans in a small pan with the cumin and a pinch of salt.
Dice the pepper and red onion, and cut the oranges into segments.
Spoon the quinoa into bowls, top with the beans, pepper, onion and orange, then finish with lime juice and oil.

recipes.title: Chard, White Bean & Potato Soup
recipes.intro: A simple, soothing soup with soft potatoes and silky greens.
recipes.whyThisPhase: White beans and chard are featured Menstrual foods for iron, and the lemon at the end adds vitamin C.
steps: Soften the chopped onion in the oil for 5 minutes, then add the garlic and diced potatoes.
Pour in the stock and simmer for 12 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Add the drained beans and the shredded chard, stalks first, and cook for 5 minutes.
Season, add a squeeze of lemon and serve.

recipes.title: Miso, Tempeh & Mushroom Noodle Bowl
recipes.intro: A savoury noodle broth that comes together in one pan.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Tempeh and kale are featured Menstrual foods for iron, alongside miso and mushrooms for a warm, savoury broth.
steps: Slice the tempeh and mushrooms and fry in the oil for 6 minutes until golden, with the grated ginger for the last minute.
Add 3 cups (700 ml) water and bring to a simmer, then stir in the kale for 2 minutes.
Cook the noodles separately according to the packet and divide between bowls.
Whisk the miso with a ladle of hot broth, stir it back in off the heat, and pour over the noodles with sliced spring onions.

recipes.title: Cinnamon Quinoa Porridge
recipes.intro: A creamy, gluten-free porridge for slower mornings.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Quinoa and pumpkin seeds are featured Menstrual foods for iron, with blueberries adding a little vitamin C.
steps: Rinse the quinoa and put it in a pan with the milk and cinnamon.
Simmer gently for 18 to 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft and creamy.
Spoon into bowls and top with blueberries, pumpkin seeds and maple syrup.

recipes.title: Sardine, Spinach & Lemon Toast
recipes.intro: A quick, tinned-fish lunch that needs barely any cooking.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Sardines and spinach are featured Menstrual foods for iron, with tomato and lemon adding vitamin C.
steps: Toast the bread.
Slice the tomatoes and pile them onto the toast with the spinach.
Break the sardines over the top, then squeeze over the lemon and add black pepper.

recipes.title: Garlic Tomato Mussels
recipes.intro: A bowl of mussels in a tomato broth with bread for mopping up.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Mussels are one of the foods Moon Cycle features for iron in the Menstrual phase, and the tomato broth adds vitamin C.
steps: Rinse the mussels and discard any that stay open when tapped or have broken shells.
Soften the chopped onion in the oil for 4 minutes, then add the garlic, chilli flakes and tomatoes and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the mussels, cover and cook for 4 to 5 minutes, shaking the pan, until the shells open. Discard any that stay closed.
Stir in the spinach until it wilts and serve with the bread.

recipes.title: Warm Beet, Orange & Kale Salad
recipes.intro: Ready-cooked beets make this a fifteen-minute lunch.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Kale and cashews are featured Menstrual foods for plant iron, and the orange adds vitamin C; beets bring colour and sweetness.
steps: Toast the cashews in a dry pan for 3 minutes, then roughly chop.
Remove the tough stalks from the kale, shred it and massage with the oil and a pinch of salt.
Cut the beetroot into wedges and the oranges into segments, saving any juice.
Toss everything with the vinegar and orange juice and serve.

recipes.title: Papaya, Kiwi & Orange Bowl
recipes.intro: A bright fruit bowl for breakfast or a snack, no cooking at all.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Papaya, kiwi and orange are vitamin C-rich Menstrual foods that sit well beside iron-rich meals, and pumpkin seeds add a little iron.
steps: Peel and cube the papaya and kiwi, and cut the oranges into segments, saving any juice.
Toss gently with the lime juice and the saved orange juice in a bowl.
Top with the pumpkin seeds and serve.

recipes.title: Zucchini & Feta Herb Frittata
recipes.intro: A light frittata that is good hot, warm or cold.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Eggs, zucchini and feta are featured Follicular foods: a quick, light meal that is easy to make fresh.
steps: Slice the zucchini and spring onions and fry in the oil in an ovenproof pan for 4 minutes.
Beat the eggs with pepper and crumble in the feta.
Pour into the pan and cook gently for 5 minutes until the edges set.
Finish under a hot grill for 3 to 4 minutes until golden, then cut into wedges.

recipes.title: Lemon Chicken & Green Bean Tray Bake
recipes.intro: One tray, little washing up, and a bright lemony finish.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Chicken, green beans and carrots are featured Follicular foods; a simple tray bake that suits fresh, uncomplicated cooking.
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Slice the carrots into batons and toss them on a tray with half the oil.
Add the chicken with the garlic, oregano, lemon zest and the rest of the oil, and roast for 10 minutes.
Add the trimmed green beans, turn everything over and roast for 12 to 15 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Squeeze over the lemon juice and serve from the tray.

recipes.title: Tuna, Pea & Lemon Pasta
recipes.intro: A pantry-friendly pasta that is on the table in twenty minutes.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Canned tuna, peas and arugula are featured Follicular foods, making a quick, light pasta from the cupboard and freezer.
steps: Cook the pasta in salted water; add the peas for the last 3 minutes.
Drain, keeping a mug of the cooking water.
Toss with the flaked tuna, the lemon zest and juice, the oil and a splash of cooking water.
Fold through the arugula and season with pepper.

recipes.title: Crumb-Topped Haddock with Minted Peas
recipes.intro: Flaky fish under a crisp oat-bran crust, with fresh minty peas.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Haddock, peas and oat bran are featured Follicular foods; a light, quick-cooked fish dinner.
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Put the fish on a lined tray and brush with half the oil.
Mix the oat bran with the lemon zest, salt and pepper, and press it onto the fish.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes until the fish flakes and the crumb is golden.
Meanwhile, simmer the peas for 3 minutes, drain and crush lightly with the mint, the rest of the oil and a squeeze of lemon.

recipes.title: Pan-Fried Trout with Cabbage & Pomegranate Slaw
recipes.intro: Crisp-skinned trout with a crunchy, jewelled slaw.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Trout, cabbage, carrot and pomegranate are all featured Follicular foods; fresh, crunchy and quick.
steps: Shred the cabbage finely and grate the carrot.
Mix the yogurt with the lemon juice and a pinch of salt, then toss through the slaw with the pomegranate seeds.
Season the trout and fry skin-side down in the oil for 4 minutes, then flip for 1 to 2 minutes.
Serve the fish on the slaw.

recipes.title: Nectarine & Plum Yogurt Bowl
recipes.intro: A cool breakfast bowl that is as good with whatever stone fruit is in season.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Yogurt, nectarines, plums, pecans and flaxseed are all featured Follicular foods, for a fresh no-cook breakfast.
steps: Stone and slice the nectarines and plums.
Spoon the yogurt into two bowls and stir in the flaxseed.
Top with the fruit and roughly chopped pecans.

recipes.title: Avocado, Egg & Arugula Toast
recipes.intro: A café-style breakfast in under fifteen minutes.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Avocado, eggs and arugula are featured Follicular foods, for a fresh and quick breakfast.
steps: Boil the eggs for 7 minutes (for jammy yolks), then cool under cold water and peel.
Toast the bread. Mash the avocado with the lemon juice and salt.
Spread the avocado on the toast and top with arugula.
Halve the eggs over the top and sprinkle with chilli flakes.

recipes.title: Hummus Crunch Wrap
recipes.intro: A no-cook, packable wrap with a tangy crunch.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Hummus, carrot, lettuce and sauerkraut are featured Follicular foods, making a fresh wrap that needs no cooking.
steps: Spread the hummus over the wraps.
Grate the carrot and layer over the hummus with the lettuce and sauerkraut.
Roll tightly, cut in half and serve.

recipes.title: Farro & Black-Eyed Pea Salad
recipes.intro: A hearty make-ahead salad that gets better as it sits.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Farro, black-eyed peas and feta are featured Follicular foods, with plenty of fresh vegetables.
steps: Simmer the farro in plenty of salted water for 20 to 25 minutes until tender, then drain and cool slightly.
Dice the cucumber and tomatoes and chop the parsley.
Toss the farro with the drained peas, vegetables, parsley, oil and lemon juice.
Crumble over the feta and season.

recipes.title: Salmon, Bok Choy & Rice Bowl
recipes.intro: A cupboard-friendly rice bowl with fresh crunch.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Canned salmon, bok choy and carrot are featured Follicular foods, for a light, quick rice bowl.
steps: Cook the rice according to the packet.
Halve the bok choy and stir-fry in the oil for 3 minutes with the carrot cut into thin matchsticks.
Add the tamari and 2 tablespoons of water and cook for 1 minute more.
Serve over the rice with the flaked salmon (bones are soft and edible) and a drizzle of sesame oil.

recipes.title: Prawn, Mango & Cucumber Rice Bowl
recipes.intro: A cool, colourful bowl of rice, fruit and crisp vegetables.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Shrimp, mango, cucumber and red pepper are featured Ovulatory foods: crisp, fresh and light.
steps: Cook the rice and let it cool for a few minutes.
Dice the mango, cucumber and pepper.
Mix the lime juice with the oil and chilli flakes.
Divide the rice between bowls, top with the prawns and diced fruit and vegetables, and spoon over the dressing.

recipes.title: Strawberry, Ricotta & Pistachio Toast
recipes.intro: Sweet, creamy and crunchy, and ready in minutes.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Strawberries, ricotta and pistachios are featured Ovulatory foods for a fresh, light breakfast.
steps: Toast the bread.
Spread generously with the ricotta.
Top with sliced strawberries and chopped pistachios, then drizzle with honey.

recipes.title: Watermelon, Cucumber & Tomato Salad
recipes.intro: A juicy, hydrating salad for hot days, as a light lunch or a side.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Watermelon, cucumber, tomato and almonds are all featured Ovulatory foods: crisp, fresh and hydrating.
steps: Cut the watermelon, cucumber and tomatoes into bite-sized chunks.
Toss with the torn mint, lime juice, oil and a pinch of salt.
Scatter over the roughly chopped almonds and serve straight away.

recipes.title: Sesame Tofu & Snap Pea Stir-Fry
recipes.intro: A fast, crunchy stir-fry for a weeknight.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Tofu, sugar snap peas, bean sprouts and red pepper are featured Ovulatory foods for a quick-cooked, crisp meal.
steps: Cook the rice according to the packet.
Press the tofu dry, cube it and fry in the oil for 5 minutes until golden, then set aside.
Stir-fry the sliced pepper, snap peas and grated ginger for 3 minutes, then add the sprouts for 1 minute.
Return the tofu, add the tamari and sesame seeds, toss and serve over rice.

recipes.title: Lemon Sea Bass with Asparagus & Tomatoes
recipes.intro: A light fish dinner on a single tray.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Sea bass, asparagus and tomatoes are featured Ovulatory foods for a light, quick-cooked meal.
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the trimmed asparagus and tomatoes with half the oil on a tray and roast for 5 minutes.
Nestle in the seasoned fish, drizzle with the rest of the oil and add lemon slices.
Roast for 8 to 10 minutes until the fish is opaque and flakes easily.
Scatter over roughly chopped hazelnuts and squeeze over the roasted lemon.

recipes.title: Crab & Cucumber Lettuce Cups
recipes.intro: Cool, crunchy cups that need no cooking.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Crab, celery, radish, cucumber and pickles are featured Ovulatory foods: crisp, cool and light.
steps: Finely dice the celery, radishes and gherkins.
Mix with the crab, yogurt, lemon juice and pepper.
Spoon into the separated lettuce leaves and serve.

recipes.title: Peach & Raspberry Kefir Bowl
recipes.intro: A cool, tangy bowl you can mix the night before.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Kefir, peaches, raspberries and almonds are featured Ovulatory foods, making a fresh, no-cook breakfast.
steps: Stir the oats into the kefir and leave for 10 minutes, or overnight in the fridge.
Slice the peaches.
Spoon into bowls and top with the peaches, raspberries and chopped almonds.

recipes.title: Cottage Cheese, Pineapple & Mandarin Bowl
recipes.intro: A sweet-and-savoury snack bowl that takes five minutes.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Cottage cheese, pineapple, mandarins and hazelnuts are all featured Ovulatory foods, for a light, fresh snack.
steps: Cut the pineapple into small chunks and peel and segment the mandarins.
Spoon the cottage cheese into bowls.
Top with the fruit and chopped hazelnuts.

recipes.title: Red Cabbage, Apricot & Chickpea Salad
recipes.intro: A crunchy, sweet-tart salad that holds up well in a lunchbox.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Red cabbage, apricots, celery and pistachios are featured Ovulatory foods, with chickpeas for substance; crisp and colourful.
steps: Shred the cabbage finely and slice the celery.
Stone and slice the apricots and drain the chickpeas.
Whisk the oil, lemon juice, cumin and salt, and toss through everything.
Scatter over the chopped pistachios.

recipes.title: Cherry, Melon & Mint Fruit Salad
recipes.intro: A fresh fruit salad for sharing, with a squeeze of lime.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Sweet cherries, cantaloupe and honeydew are featured Ovulatory foods: juicy, light and hydrating.
steps: Pit and halve the cherries and cut the melons into bite-sized pieces.
Toss together with the torn mint and the lime juice.
Chill for 10 minutes if you have time, then serve.

recipes.title: Baked Apple & Walnut Oatmeal
recipes.intro: A cosy baked oatmeal you can slice and reheat through the week.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Oats, apples, banana and walnuts are featured Luteal foods: a hearty, filling make-ahead breakfast.
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C) and grease a baking dish.
Mash the bananas and stir in the milk, oats, cinnamon, baking powder and grated apple.
Pour into the dish, scatter over the chopped walnuts and bake for 30 minutes until set and golden.
Cut into squares and serve warm.

recipes.title: Chia, Pear & Yogurt Pots
recipes.intro: Layered pots that are filling and can be made ahead.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Greek yogurt, chia seeds, pears, nut butter and sunflower seeds are featured Luteal foods, adding protein and fibre to breakfast.
steps: Stir the chia seeds into the yogurt and leave for 10 minutes to thicken.
Dice the pears.
Layer the yogurt and pears into glasses or jars, then top with spoonfuls of nut butter and sunflower seeds.

recipes.title: Red Lentil & Pumpkin Soup
recipes.intro: A velvety, lightly spiced soup that needs no blending skills.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Red lentils and pumpkin are featured Luteal foods; lentils bring protein and fibre for a filling, warming soup.
steps: Soften the chopped onion and carrot in the oil for 5 minutes, then add the garlic and curry powder for 1 minute.
Add the diced pumpkin, lentils and stock and simmer for 20 minutes.
Blend until smooth, or mash with a fork for a chunkier soup.
Season to taste and serve.

recipes.title: Tahini Chickpea & Sweet Potato Tray
recipes.intro: A roast-everything dinner with a lemony tahini drizzle.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Chickpeas and sweet potato are featured Luteal foods; chickpeas add protein and fibre, and roasting makes the tray hearty and filling.
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Cut the sweet potatoes into chunks and the cauliflower into florets.
Toss with the drained chickpeas, oil, paprika and salt on a large tray and roast for 30 minutes, turning once.
Stir the tahini with the lemon juice and a little water until pourable.
Drizzle over the tray and serve.

recipes.title: Salmon, Edamame & Brown Rice Bowl
recipes.intro: A satisfying bowl with a tangy kimchi kick.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Salmon, edamame, brown rice and kimchi are featured Luteal foods; salmon and edamame bring protein and the rice slower-digesting carbohydrate for a satisfying bowl.
steps: Cook the brown rice according to the packet, adding the edamame for the last 3 minutes.
Brush the salmon with the oil and tamari and fry, skin-side down, for 4 minutes, then flip for 2 minutes.
Slice the cucumber.
Divide the rice and edamame between bowls and top with the salmon, cucumber and kimchi.

recipes.title: Turkey, Pinto Bean & Squash Skillet
recipes.intro: A one-pan supper with smoky paprika.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Turkey, pinto beans and squash are featured Luteal foods; the beans and turkey bring protein and fibre for a hearty one-pan meal.
steps: Brown the turkey in the oil for 5 minutes, breaking it up, then add the onion and squash and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, paprika and cumin for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, drained beans and about ½ cup (100 ml) water, cover and simmer for 15 minutes until the squash is tender.
Season and serve.

recipes.title: Baked Cod with Lima Beans & Tomatoes
recipes.intro: Tender white fish baked on a bed of creamy beans.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Cod, lima beans and artichokes are featured Luteal foods; the beans add protein and fibre alongside the fish.
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Mix the drained lima beans, tomatoes, sliced artichokes, garlic and oil in a baking dish with a pinch of salt.
Bake for 8 minutes.
Nestle in the seasoned cod and bake for 10 to 12 minutes until the fish flakes.
Scatter over the parsley and serve.

recipes.title: Pork, Barley & Parsnip Stew
recipes.intro: A slow, grounding stew for a day you have time to let it bubble.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Pork, barley and parsnips are featured Luteal foods; the barley adds fibre and slower-digesting carbohydrate to a hearty, one-pot stew.
steps: Brown the pork in the oil in a large pot for 6 minutes, then add the chopped onion and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the barley, thyme and stock, bring to the boil, cover and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the diced parsnips and carrots and simmer for another 20 to 25 minutes until the barley and pork are tender.
Season and serve in deep bowls.

recipes.title: Roast Squash, Bulgur & Goat Cheese Salad
recipes.intro: A warm salad that works for lunch the next day, too.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Squash, bulgur, goat cheese and walnuts are featured Luteal foods; bulgur brings fibre and slower-digesting carbohydrate to a warm, filling salad.
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the squash with half the oil, the cumin and salt and roast for 25 minutes.
Meanwhile, cover the bulgur with boiling water in a bowl for 15 minutes, then drain.
Mix the bulgur with the lemon juice, the rest of the oil and the chopped parsley.
Top with the roasted squash, crumbled goat cheese and chopped walnuts.

recipes.title: Spiced Lamb & Split Pea One-Pot
recipes.intro: A slow-cooked, warmly spiced one-pot for a quiet evening.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Lamb and split peas are featured Luteal foods; the split peas add protein and fibre to a long, slow-cooked and filling one-pot meal.
steps: Brown the lamb in the oil in a heavy pot for 6 minutes, then add the chopped onion and carrots and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, cumin and coriander for 1 minute.
Add the rinsed split peas and stock, bring to the boil, then cover and simmer gently for 45 to 50 minutes, stirring now and then, until the lamb and peas are soft.
Season and serve with flatbread or rice.

recipes.title: Warm Wild Rice & Blueberry Breakfast Bowl
recipes.intro: A cosy breakfast bowl; cook extra wild rice and keep it in the fridge for the week.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Wild rice, blueberries and sesame seeds are featured Menstrual foods, and the berries add a little vitamin C to a warm, comforting breakfast.
steps: Rinse the wild rice and simmer it in plenty of water for 35 to 40 minutes, until the grains split. Drain.
Return it to the pan with the milk and cinnamon and warm gently for 5 minutes.
Spoon into bowls and top with blueberries, sesame seeds and a little maple syrup.

recipes.title: Mushroom & Chard Egg Scramble on Toast
recipes.intro: Soft eggs with savoury mushrooms and greens on toast.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Chard is a featured Menstrual food for plant iron, and mushrooms and eggs make it a quick, savoury breakfast.
steps: Slice the mushrooms and fry in the oil for 4 minutes with the chopped garlic.
Add the shredded chard and cook for 2 minutes until wilted.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt, pour in and stir gently for 2 to 3 minutes until just set. Toast the bread.
Pile the eggs on the toast and serve.

recipes.title: Kiwi, Blueberry & Cashew Yogurt Bowl
recipes.intro: A no-cook breakfast bowl with tangy fruit and a salty crunch.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Kiwi and blueberries add vitamin C, and cashews add some plant iron, in a quick Menstrual-phase breakfast.
steps: Peel and slice the kiwi and roughly chop the cashews.
Spoon the yogurt into two bowls.
Top with the kiwi, blueberries, cashews and sesame seeds.

recipes.title: Black Bean & Yellow Pepper Breakfast Tortillas
recipes.intro: Warm, savoury and entirely plant-based, with a squeeze of lime.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Black beans are a featured Menstrual food for plant iron, and the yellow pepper and lime add vitamin C.
steps: Dice the pepper and fry in the oil for 4 minutes, then add the sliced spring onions.
Add the drained beans and cumin and warm through for 4 minutes, mashing a few beans.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan or the microwave.
Fill with the bean mixture and finish with lime juice.

recipes.title: Broccoli, White Bean & Miso Soup
recipes.intro: A quick green soup with a gentle savoury depth from miso.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Broccoli, white beans and miso are featured Menstrual foods, with white beans bringing plant iron and broccoli vitamin C.
steps: Soften the sliced garlic in the oil for 1 minute, then add the diced potatoes and the stock and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the broccoli florets and cook for 5 minutes until tender.
Stir in the drained beans, then blend about half the soup for a creamy texture.
Take off the heat, whisk the miso with a ladle of hot soup, stir it back in and season with pepper.

recipes.title: Brussels Sprout, Beet & Quinoa Salad
recipes.intro: A warm, earthy salad with a bright orange dressing.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Brussels sprouts and oranges add vitamin C, and quinoa and sesame seeds are featured Menstrual foods, alongside sweet beets.
steps: Rinse the quinoa and simmer in twice its volume of water for 15 minutes, then drain.
Shred the Brussels sprouts and fry in half the oil for 6 to 8 minutes until browned and tender.
Whisk the orange juice and zest with the vinegar, the rest of the oil and a pinch of salt.
Toss the quinoa, sprouts and diced beetroot with the dressing and top with sesame seeds.

recipes.title: Kidney Bean & Collard Green Wraps
recipes.intro: Sturdy collard leaves stand in for a tortilla.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Collard greens and kidney beans are featured Menstrual foods for iron, and the pepper and lime add vitamin C.
steps: Trim the thick stalks from the collard leaves and dip them in boiling water for 1 minute, then pat dry.
Mash the drained beans with the cumin, a pinch of salt and half the lime juice.
Spread the beans over the leaves and add sliced pepper and avocado.
Squeeze over the rest of the lime, then fold in the sides and roll up.

recipes.title: Grapefruit, Beet & Spinach Salad with Cashews
recipes.intro: A juicy, jewel-coloured salad that needs no cooking.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Grapefruit is rich in vitamin C, and spinach and cashews are featured Menstrual foods for plant iron.
steps: Cut away the peel and pith of the grapefruit and slice into segments, saving the juice.
Cut the beetroot into wedges and roughly chop the cashews.
Whisk the saved juice with the oil, vinegar and salt.
Toss the spinach with the dressing, top with the beetroot, grapefruit and cashews.

recipes.title: Garlic Clam & Kale Spaghetti
recipes.intro: A pantry pasta made with canned clams.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Clams are a featured Menstrual food for iron, and kale and lemon add vitamin C.
steps: Cook the spaghetti in salted water; add the shredded kale for the last 2 minutes. Keep a mug of the water.
Meanwhile, warm the oil with the sliced garlic and chilli flakes for 2 minutes.
Add the clams with their juice and warm through for 3 minutes.
Toss the drained pasta and kale through the clams with a splash of cooking water and the lemon juice.

recipes.title: Roasted Broccoli, Potato & Anchovy Tray
recipes.intro: One tray; the anchovies melt into the oil and season everything.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Anchovies are a featured Menstrual food for iron, and broccoli, potato and lemon add vitamin C to a hands-off tray bake.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Cut the potatoes into chunks and toss with half the oil on a large tray; roast for 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, warm the rest of the oil with the anchovies and sliced garlic until the anchovies dissolve.
Add the broccoli florets to the tray, pour over the anchovy oil and roast for 12 to 15 minutes.
Squeeze over the lemon, add pepper and serve from the tray.

recipes.title: Easy Oyster & Spinach Stew
recipes.intro: A simple, warming stew made with canned oysters; serve with toast.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Oysters are a featured Menstrual food for iron, and spinach adds more to a simple, warming stew.
steps: Soften the finely chopped onion in the butter for 4 minutes.
Add the milk and the oysters with their liquid and warm gently for 5 minutes without boiling.
Stir in the spinach until wilted and season with pepper.
Serve in bowls with toasted whole-grain bread.

recipes.title: Beef, Brussels Sprout & Potato Tray
recipes.intro: Seared steak strips over crisp roasted potatoes and sprouts.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Beef is a featured Menstrual food for iron, and Brussels sprouts add vitamin C alongside hearty potatoes.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the diced potatoes with half the oil and roast for 15 minutes.
Add the halved sprouts and garlic cloves and roast for 10 minutes more.
Slice the steak, season and sear in the rest of the oil in a hot pan for 2 to 3 minutes each side.
Serve the beef over the roasted vegetables.

recipes.title: Eggplant, Lentil & Collard Stew
recipes.intro: A slow, spiced vegan stew that gets better the next day.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Lentils and collard greens are featured Menstrual foods for plant iron, with eggplant making the stew soft and filling.
steps: Cube the eggplant and brown in the oil for 6 minutes, then add the chopped onion, garlic and grated ginger for 4 minutes.
Stir in the cumin, lentils and stock, bring to the boil and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the shredded collards and cook for 5 minutes until tender.
Season and serve.

recipes.title: Sesame Eggplant & Tempeh Rice Bowl
recipes.intro: Glossy sesame-tamari eggplant and crisp tempeh over rice.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Tempeh and sesame seeds are featured Menstrual foods, with tempeh adding plant iron and the green pepper vitamin C.
steps: Cook the rice according to the packet.
Fry the cubed eggplant in the oil for 8 minutes until golden, then add the sliced tempeh and pepper for 5 minutes.
Add the tamari and a splash of water and cook for 2 minutes until glossy.
Serve over the rice, scattered with the sesame seeds.

recipes.title: Mushroom & Wild Rice Soup
recipes.intro: A slow, earthy soup that is worth the simmer.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Wild rice and kale are featured Menstrual foods, with kale adding some plant iron and vitamin C to a warming mushroom soup.
steps: Soften the chopped onion and sliced mushrooms in the oil for 8 minutes, then add the garlic and thyme.
Add the rinsed wild rice and the stock, bring to the boil, cover and simmer for 35 to 40 minutes until the grains split.
Stir in the shredded kale for the last 5 minutes.
Season and serve.

recipes.title: Grape, Papaya & Cashew Fruit Cup
recipes.intro: A juicy snack cup with a little crunch.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Papaya is rich in vitamin C, and grapes and cashews are featured Menstrual foods, for an easy snack.
steps: Halve the grapes and cube the papaya.
Toss with the lime juice in two cups or small bowls.
Top with roughly chopped cashews.

recipes.title: Sesame Beet Dip with Pepper Strips
recipes.intro: A vivid pink dip for dunking crisp peppers.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Beets and sesame seeds are featured Menstrual foods, and the peppers add vitamin C to an easy dipping snack.
steps: Blend or finely mash the beetroot with the tahini, lemon juice, garlic, oil and salt until smooth.
Spoon into a bowl and scatter over the sesame seeds.
Cut the peppers into strips and serve alongside for dipping.

recipes.title: Oat Bran Porridge with Plum & Flaxseed
recipes.intro: A fast, creamy porridge that is ready in about ten minutes.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Oat bran, plums, flaxseed and pecans are all featured Follicular foods, making a fresh, quick breakfast.
steps: Stir the oat bran into the milk in a small pan and cook over medium heat for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring, until thick.
Slice the plums and chop the pecans.
Spoon into bowls and top with the plums, flaxseed, pecans and cinnamon.

recipes.title: Egg & Pea Breakfast Fried Rice
recipes.intro: A savoury breakfast that makes good use of leftover rice.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Eggs and green peas are featured Follicular foods, making a quick, light savoury breakfast.
steps: Heat the oil in a wide pan and fry the sliced spring onions for 1 minute.
Add the rice and peas and stir-fry for 4 minutes until hot.
Push the rice to one side, scramble the beaten eggs in the gap, then mix everything together.
Season with the tamari and serve.

recipes.title: Plum, Pomegranate & Brazil Nut Yogurt Bowl
recipes.intro: A tart, juicy yogurt bowl with a rich nutty finish.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Plums, pomegranate and Brazil nuts are featured Follicular foods, for a fresh no-cook breakfast.
steps: Stone and slice the plums and roughly chop the Brazil nuts.
Spoon the yogurt into two bowls.
Top with the plums, pomegranate seeds and nuts.

recipes.title: Turnip & Zucchini Egg Hash
recipes.intro: A crisp skillet hash with eggs cooked on top.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Turnip, zucchini and eggs are featured Follicular foods, making a light, savoury skillet breakfast.
steps: Grate the turnips and zucchini and squeeze out the liquid in a clean towel.
Fry in the oil for 8 minutes, turning, until golden at the edges, adding the sliced spring onions for the last 2 minutes.
Make four wells, crack in the eggs, cover and cook for 3 to 4 minutes.
Season and scatter over the parsley.

recipes.title: Savoury Napa Cabbage & Egg Pancakes
recipes.intro: Crisp-edged savoury pancakes for a weekend brunch.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Napa cabbage and eggs are featured Follicular foods, making a light, quick savoury pancake.
steps: Shred the cabbage finely and slice the spring onions.
Beat the eggs with the flour, tamari and a splash of water, then stir in the vegetables.
Fry spoonfuls in the oil over medium heat for 3 minutes each side until golden.
Serve hot, with extra tamari for dipping.

recipes.title: Canned Salmon & Green Bean Salad
recipes.intro: A pantry salad with jammy eggs and crisp beans.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Canned salmon, green beans, eggs and lettuce are featured Follicular foods, for a light, quick lunch.
steps: Boil the eggs for 7 minutes, adding the trimmed green beans for the last 3 minutes. Cool under cold water.
Peel and quarter the eggs; flake the salmon, removing any large bones.
Whisk the lemon juice with the oil and a pinch of salt.
Toss the lettuce, beans and salmon with the dressing and top with the eggs.

recipes.title: Chicken & Napa Cabbage Noodle Slaw
recipes.intro: A crunchy, tangy slaw with poached chicken and rice noodles.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Chicken and napa cabbage are featured Follicular foods, making a fresh, light bowl.
steps: Simmer the chicken in a pan of water for 12 minutes until cooked through, then shred.
Soak the noodles in boiling water for 4 minutes and drain.
Shred the cabbage and slice the spring onions; whisk the tamari, vinegar and grated ginger.
Toss everything together and serve.

recipes.title: Black-Eyed Pea, Turnip & Zucchini Soup
recipes.intro: A light, mild vegan soup that is easy to batch-cook.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Black-eyed peas, turnip and zucchini are featured Follicular foods, making a light, fresh-tasting soup.
steps: Soften the chopped onion in the oil for 4 minutes, then add the garlic and diced turnips.
Add the stock and simmer for 12 minutes, then add the diced zucchini and the drained peas for 6 minutes.
Season, stir in the chopped parsley and serve.

recipes.title: Hummus, Pomegranate & Cabbage Mezze Plate
recipes.intro: A no-cook sharing plate for a relaxed lunch.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Hummus, pomegranate and cabbage are featured Follicular foods, making a fresh, light assembly lunch.
steps: Shred the cabbage finely and toss with the lemon juice, a drizzle of oil and a pinch of salt.
Spoon the hummus onto a plate and scatter with pomegranate seeds.
Warm the pita, cut into wedges and serve with the slaw and olives.

recipes.title: Pollock Tacos with Cabbage Slaw
recipes.intro: Mild, flaky fish tacos with a crunchy slaw and avocado.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Pollock, cabbage and avocado are featured Follicular foods, making a light, quick fish dinner.
steps: Shred the cabbage and toss with half the lime juice and a pinch of salt.
Rub the fish with cumin and salt and fry in the oil for 3 to 4 minutes each side, then break into chunks.
Warm the tortillas and slice the avocado.
Fill with fish, slaw and avocado and squeeze over the rest of the lime.

recipes.title: Seared Scallops with Bok Choy & Rice Noodles
recipes.intro: A short, special-occasion dinner that is on the table in 20 minutes.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Scallops and bok choy are featured Follicular foods, making a light, quick-cooked dinner.
steps: Soak the noodles in boiling water for 4 minutes, then drain.
Pat the scallops dry and sear in half the oil in a very hot pan for 1 to 2 minutes each side. Set aside.
Stir-fry the halved bok choy and grated ginger in the rest of the oil for 3 minutes, then add the tamari and noodles.
Serve the scallops on top.

recipes.title: Chicken, Farro & Zucchini Skillet
recipes.intro: A one-pan supper with chewy grains and a lemony finish.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Chicken, farro, zucchini and arugula are featured Follicular foods, making a fresh, one-pan dinner.
steps: Brown the sliced chicken in the oil in a wide pan for 6 minutes.
Add the farro and stock, cover and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the sliced zucchini and cook for 5 minutes until the farro is tender and the stock is absorbed.
Stir through the arugula and lemon juice and season.

recipes.title: Pecan-Crusted Trout with Green Beans
recipes.intro: Oven-baked trout under a buttery pecan crust.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Trout, pecans and green beans are featured Follicular foods, making a light, quick fish dinner.
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F (400°F (200°C)). Finely chop the pecans and mix with the lemon zest, a little oil and salt.
Put the trout on a lined tray, season and press the pecan mixture on top.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes until the fish flakes.
Meanwhile, steam or boil the green beans for 5 minutes, dress with oil and lemon juice, and serve.

recipes.title: Date, Brazil Nut & Flax Bites
recipes.intro: No-bake bites that keep for a week in the fridge.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Brazil nuts, flaxseed and oat bran are featured Follicular foods, rolled into an easy no-bake snack.
steps: Blend or finely chop the Brazil nuts, then mash in the dates, flaxseed, oat bran and salt until it sticks together.
Roll into small balls with damp hands.
Chill for 20 minutes before serving.

recipes.title: Mango & Raspberry Kefir Smoothie Bowl
recipes.intro: A thick, tangy fruit bowl you can eat with a spoon.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Kefir, mango, raspberries and pistachios are featured Ovulatory foods, making a bright, cool breakfast.
steps: Blend the kefir with the peeled mango and half the raspberries until thick and smooth.
Pour into two bowls.
Top with the remaining raspberries and chopped pistachios.

recipes.title: Ricotta Pancakes with Strawberries
recipes.intro: Soft, fluffy pancakes for a leisurely morning.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Ricotta and strawberries are featured Ovulatory foods, for a fresh, bright weekend breakfast.
steps: Whisk the ricotta, eggs and milk, then fold in the flour and baking powder to a thick batter.
Cook spoonfuls in a lightly oiled pan for 2 to 3 minutes each side until golden.
Slice the strawberries and serve over the pancakes.

recipes.title: Tofu Scramble with Asparagus & Red Pepper
recipes.intro: A plant-based scramble with fresh spring flavours.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Tofu, asparagus and red pepper are featured Ovulatory foods, making a quick, colourful breakfast.
steps: Slice the asparagus and pepper and fry in the oil for 5 minutes.
Crumble in the tofu with the turmeric and salt and cook for 5 minutes, stirring.
Stir in the sliced spring onions and serve.

recipes.title: Apricot & Hazelnut Overnight Oats
recipes.intro: Mix it in the evening and breakfast is ready.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Apricots and hazelnuts are featured Ovulatory foods, making a fresh, make-ahead breakfast.
steps: Stir the oats and milk together in a jar or bowl and refrigerate overnight.
In the morning, stone and slice the apricots and chop the hazelnuts.
Top the oats with the apricots and hazelnuts.

recipes.title: Shrimp & Sugar Snap Pea Noodle Salad
recipes.intro: A cool, crunchy noodle salad with a lime and tamari dressing.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Shrimp, sugar snap peas and radishes are featured Ovulatory foods, making a crisp, cool noodle salad.
steps: Soak the noodles in boiling water for 4 minutes, drain and rinse under cold water.
Slice the snap peas and radishes thinly.
Whisk the lime juice with the tamari.
Toss the noodles, vegetables and prawns with the dressing.

recipes.title: Crab, Red Cabbage & Pickle Sandwich
recipes.intro: A crunchy open sandwich with a tangy yogurt dressing.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Crab, red cabbage and pickles are featured Ovulatory foods, making a crisp, fresh sandwich.
steps: Shred the red cabbage and dice the gherkins.
Mix with the crab, yogurt, lemon juice and pepper.
Toast the bread and pile the crab mixture on top.

recipes.title: Cold Sesame Tofu & Bean Sprout Soba
recipes.intro: Chilled buckwheat noodles with crisp tofu and sprouts.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Tofu and bean sprouts are featured Ovulatory foods, making a chilled, quick-cooked noodle lunch.
steps: Cook the soba according to the packet, then rinse under cold water and drain.
Fry the cubed tofu in the oil for 6 minutes until golden.
Toss the noodles with the tamari, sprouts and sliced spring onions.
Top with the tofu and sesame seeds.

recipes.title: Peach, Ricotta & Arugula Flatbread
recipes.intro: Sweet peach, creamy ricotta and a peppery finish on warm naan.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Peach, ricotta and arugula are featured Ovulatory foods, making a fresh, bright flatbread lunch.
steps: Warm the naan in a hot pan or oven for 3 minutes.
Spread with ricotta and top with sliced peaches.
Drizzle with honey, add pepper and finish with the arugula.

recipes.title: Pan-Seared Sea Bass with Pineapple Slaw
recipes.intro: Crisp-skinned fish with a sweet-sharp slaw.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Sea bass, pineapple and red cabbage are featured Ovulatory foods, making a bright, quick-cooked dinner.
steps: Shred the cabbage, dice the pineapple and toss with the lime juice, torn mint and a pinch of salt.
Season the fish and fry skin-side down in the oil for 4 minutes until crisp.
Flip and cook for 2 minutes more.
Serve the fish on the slaw.

recipes.title: Shrimp & Asparagus Lemon Pasta
recipes.intro: A fast, fresh pasta with spring vegetables.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Shrimp and asparagus are featured Ovulatory foods, making a quick-cooked, bright pasta dinner.
steps: Cook the pasta in salted water; add the asparagus pieces for the last 3 minutes. Keep a mug of the water.
Fry the sliced garlic in the oil for 1 minute, add the prawns and cook for 3 minutes until pink.
Toss the drained pasta and asparagus with the prawns, lemon zest and juice and a splash of cooking water.

recipes.title: Tofu Banh Mi Bowl with Pickles & Radish
recipes.intro: Crisp tofu with tangy pickles over rice.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Tofu, pickles and radishes are featured Ovulatory foods, making a crisp, bright rice bowl.
steps: Cook the rice according to the packet.
Fry the cubed tofu in the oil for 6 minutes until golden, then add the tamari.
Slice the pickles, radishes and spring onions.
Serve the tofu and vegetables over the rice with a squeeze of lime.

recipes.title: Melon & Raspberry Cups with Kefir
recipes.intro: A cool, hydrating snack with a tangy kefir drizzle.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Cantaloupe, honeydew, raspberries and kefir are featured Ovulatory foods, for a cool, hydrating snack.
steps: Cut the melons into small cubes.
Divide between two glasses with the raspberries.
Pour over the kefir and top with torn mint.

recipes.title: Mandarin, Cherry & Pistachio Snack Plate
recipes.intro: A sweet and savoury snack plate in five minutes.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Mandarins, sweet cherries, pistachios and cottage cheese are featured Ovulatory foods, for a fresh, light snack.
steps: Peel and segment the mandarins.
Spoon the cottage cheese onto two plates.
Arrange the mandarins and cherries alongside and scatter over the pistachios.

recipes.title: Buckwheat Porridge with Blackberries & Mixed Nuts
recipes.intro: A nutty, cosy porridge made with buckwheat groats.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Buckwheat, blackberries and mixed nuts are featured Luteal foods, for a hearty, filling porridge.
steps: Rinse the buckwheat and simmer with the milk and about ½ cup (100 ml) water for 12 to 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft.
Chop the nuts roughly.
Spoon into bowls and top with the blackberries, nuts and cinnamon.

recipes.title: Peanut Butter, Banana & Chia Toast
recipes.intro: A filling five-minute breakfast.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Peanut butter, bananas, chia seeds and whole-grain bread are featured Luteal foods, making a filling, fast breakfast.
steps: Toast the bread.
Spread with the peanut butter and top with sliced banana.
Sprinkle over the chia seeds and chopped peanuts.

recipes.title: Fig, Goat Cheese & Walnut Toast
recipes.intro: Sweet figs and tangy goat cheese on crunchy toast.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Figs, goat cheese, walnuts and whole-grain bread are featured Luteal foods, making a simple, satisfying toast.
steps: Toast the bread and toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 2 minutes.
Spread the toast with goat cheese.
Top with sliced figs and chopped walnuts and finish with pepper.

recipes.title: Sweet Potato & Pinto Bean Breakfast Hash
recipes.intro: A hearty skillet hash with eggs on top.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Sweet potato, pinto beans and kale are featured Luteal foods, with beans adding protein and fibre to a filling breakfast.
steps: Fry the diced sweet potato and chopped onion in the oil for 12 minutes until tender and browned.
Add the drained beans, paprika and shredded kale and cook for 4 minutes.
Make four wells, crack in the eggs, cover and cook for 4 minutes.
Season and serve from the pan.

recipes.title: Pear & Barley Porridge with Sunflower Seeds
recipes.intro: A slow, chewy porridge for a cosy morning.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Barley, pears and sunflower seeds are featured Luteal foods, with barley adding fibre and slower-digesting carbohydrate to a filling porridge.
steps: Simmer the barley in the milk and 1 cup (300 ml) water for 30 to 35 minutes, stirring now and then, until tender and creamy.
Dice the pears and stir half in for the last 5 minutes.
Spoon into bowls and top with the remaining pear, sunflower seeds and cinnamon.

recipes.title: Roast Pumpkin & Mozzarella Panini
recipes.intro: A warm, melty sandwich with sweet roasted pumpkin.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Pumpkin and mozzarella are featured Luteal foods, making a warm, filling sandwich.
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F (400°F (200°C)). Slice the pumpkin and onion thinly, toss with half the oil and salt, and roast for 18 to 20 minutes.
Layer the pumpkin, onion and sliced mozzarella between the bread.
Brush the outside with the rest of the oil and toast in a hot pan for 3 minutes each side, pressing down, until golden and melted.

recipes.title: Turkey, Swiss & Apple Sandwich
recipes.intro: A crunchy, sweet-and-savoury sandwich with no cooking.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Turkey, Swiss cheese and apple are featured Luteal foods; the turkey and cheese bring protein to an easy sandwich.
steps: Core and thinly slice the apple.
Layer the turkey, cheese and apple on two slices of bread and add pepper.
Top with the remaining bread, press down and cut in half.

recipes.title: Mackerel, Lima Bean & Artichoke Salad
recipes.intro: A pantry-friendly salad of canned fish, beans and artichokes.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Mackerel, lima beans and artichokes are featured Luteal foods; the fish and beans bring protein, and the beans and artichokes fibre.
steps: Drain the beans and artichokes and quarter the artichokes.
Whisk the lemon juice, oil and salt, and toss through the beans, artichokes and chopped parsley.
Flake the mackerel over the top and serve.

recipes.title: Kimchi Fried Brown Rice with Egg
recipes.intro: A spicy, tangy fried-rice bowl with a runny egg.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Brown rice, kimchi, edamame and eggs make a filling bowl, with brown rice bringing fibre and slower-digesting carbohydrate.
steps: Fry the chopped kimchi in half the oil for 2 minutes, then add the rice and edamame and stir-fry for 5 minutes.
Fry the eggs in the rest of the oil in a separate pan until the whites are set.
Serve the rice in bowls topped with the eggs and sliced spring onions.

recipes.title: Peanut-Lime Noodle Bowl with Edamame
recipes.intro: Buckwheat noodles in a creamy peanut dressing.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Peanuts, nut butter and edamame are featured Luteal foods, and with soba noodles they bring protein and fibre to a filling noodle bowl.
steps: Cook the soba according to the packet, adding the edamame for the last 2 minutes. Drain.
Whisk the peanut butter with the lime juice, tamari and 3 tablespoons of warm water.
Toss the noodles and edamame with the dressing and the shredded cabbage.
Top with chopped peanuts.

recipes.title: Roasted Halibut with Parsnips & Lemon
recipes.intro: Tender fish over sweet roasted parsnips.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Halibut and parsnips are featured Luteal foods; the fish brings protein to a cosy, roasted dinner.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the parsnip batons and garlic with half the oil and roast for 15 minutes.
Nestle in the seasoned halibut, drizzle with the rest of the oil and add lemon slices.
Roast for 8 to 10 minutes until the fish flakes.
Scatter over the parsley and serve.

recipes.title: Baked Flounder with Buckwheat & Green Beans
recipes.intro: A light fish dish on a bed of nutty buckwheat.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Flounder, buckwheat and green beans are featured Luteal foods; the fish brings protein and the buckwheat slower-digesting carbohydrate.
steps: Simmer the rinsed buckwheat in twice its volume of water for 12 minutes, covered, then rest for 5 minutes.
Heat the oven to 400°F (400°F (200°C)) and lay the flounder on a lined tray with the trimmed beans, oil, lemon slices and salt.
Bake for 10 to 12 minutes until the fish is opaque.
Serve the fish and beans over the buckwheat.

recipes.title: Snapper, Cauliflower & Chickpea Tray
recipes.intro: A one-tray dinner with smoky roasted vegetables.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Snapper, cauliflower and chickpeas are featured Luteal foods; the fish and chickpeas bring protein, and the chickpeas fibre.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the cauliflower florets, drained chickpeas, garlic, paprika, salt and two-thirds of the oil on a tray and roast for 15 minutes.
Nestle in the seasoned snapper, drizzle with the rest of the oil and add lemon slices.
Roast for 8 to 10 minutes until the fish flakes.
Squeeze over the lemon and serve.

recipes.title: Tilapia & Pinto Bean Tacos
recipes.intro: Easy weeknight tacos with spiced fish and beans.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Tilapia and pinto beans are featured Luteal foods, and the beans add protein and fibre to a filling taco supper.
steps: Warm the drained beans with half the cumin and a splash of water for 5 minutes, mashing a few.
Season the fish with the rest of the cumin and salt and fry in the oil for 3 minutes each side, then flake.
Shred the cabbage and warm the tortillas.
Fill with beans, fish and cabbage and squeeze over the lime.

recipes.title: Pork, Apple & Sweet Potato Skillet
recipes.intro: A cosy autumn skillet that cooks in one pan.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Pork, apples and sweet potato are featured Luteal foods; the pork brings protein and the sweet potato a steady, filling carbohydrate.
steps: Fry the diced sweet potatoes in the oil for 10 minutes until starting to soften, then add the chopped onion for 4 minutes.
Push to the side, sear the seasoned pork for 3 minutes each side and slice.
Add the wedged apples and thyme and cook for 4 minutes.
Combine everything in the pan and serve.

recipes.title: Lamb Kofta Bowl with Bulgur
recipes.intro: Spiced lamb patties over bulgur with cool yogurt.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Lamb and bulgur are featured Luteal foods; the lamb brings protein and the bulgur fibre and slower-digesting carbohydrate.
steps: Cover the bulgur with boiling water in a bowl for 15 minutes, then drain.
Mix the lamb with the chopped parsley, cumin and salt and shape into small patties.
Fry in the oil for 4 minutes each side until browned and cooked through.
Toss the bulgur with lemon juice, serve the kofta on top and add the yogurt.

recipes.title: Cod, Red Lentil & Cauliflower Stew
recipes.intro: A gentle, golden stew that cooks the fish in the last few minutes.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Cod, red lentils and cauliflower are featured Luteal foods; the fish and lentils bring protein and the lentils fibre.
steps: Soften the chopped onion in the oil for 4 minutes, then add the garlic and curry powder for 1 minute.
Add the lentils, cauliflower florets and stock and simmer for 15 minutes.
Nestle in the cod chunks and cook gently for 5 to 6 minutes until the fish flakes.
Season and serve.

recipes.title: Spiced Mixed Nuts & Fig Snack Jar
recipes.intro: Warm, lightly spiced nuts to keep in a jar.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Mixed nuts, figs and sunflower seeds are featured Luteal foods, and the nuts and seeds bring protein and fibre to an easy snack.
steps: Toast the nuts and sunflower seeds in a dry pan for 5 to 6 minutes, shaking often.
Toss with the paprika, oil and a pinch of salt and let cool.
Pack into a jar and serve with sliced fresh figs.

recipes.title: Nectarine & Pecan Chia Pudding
recipes.intro: A make-ahead pudding that sets while you sleep.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Nectarines and pecans are featured Follicular foods, making a fresh, no-cook, make-ahead breakfast.
steps: Whisk the chia seeds with the almond milk, maple syrup and vanilla. Leave for 10 minutes, then whisk again to break up any clumps.
Cover and chill for at least 30 minutes, or overnight, until thick.
Slice the nectarines, roughly chop the pecans and spoon both over the pudding.

recipes.title: Black-Eyed Pea, Avocado & Sauerkraut Breakfast Bowl
recipes.intro: A savoury, plant-based breakfast bowl with a tangy crunch.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Black-eyed peas, avocado and sauerkraut are featured Follicular foods, making a savoury, fresh-tasting breakfast bowl.
steps: Warm the drained peas in the oil with the chilli flakes and a pinch of salt for 4 minutes. Warm the rice.
Divide the rice and shredded lettuce between two bowls.
Top with the peas, sliced avocado and sauerkraut and squeeze over the lemon.

recipes.title: Quinoa, Hummus & Pomegranate Bowl
recipes.intro: A colourful, gluten-free grain bowl you can eat warm or cold.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Hummus, pomegranate and cabbage are featured Follicular foods, making a fresh, light bowl with quinoa for substance.
steps: Rinse the quinoa and simmer in twice its volume of water for 15 minutes, then drain and fluff.
Shred the cabbage and toss with the lemon juice, oil and a pinch of salt.
Divide the quinoa between bowls and top with the cabbage, a spoonful of hummus, the olives and the pomegranate seeds.

recipes.title: Bok Choy, Turnip & Tofu Rice Bowl
recipes.intro: Crisp roasted turnip and tofu with quick-cooked greens, seasoned with ginger and lime.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Bok choy and turnip are featured Follicular foods, with tofu making a light, quick-cooked vegan rice bowl.
steps: Cook the rice according to the packet.
Fry the diced turnips in the oil for 8 minutes until golden, then add the cubed tofu for 5 minutes.
Add the halved bok choy and grated ginger and cook for 3 minutes until just tender.
Season with salt and lime juice and serve over the rice, scattered with the sesame seeds.

recipes.title: Stone Fruit & Brazil Nut Snack Plate
recipes.intro: A fresh, no-cook snack plate with a rich nutty finish.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Nectarines, plums, pomegranate and Brazil nuts are all featured Follicular foods, making a fresh, no-cook snack plate.
steps: Slice the nectarine and plums and arrange on two plates.
Scatter over the pomegranate seeds.
Serve with the Brazil nuts on the side.

recipes.title: Mango & Raspberry Chia Pudding
recipes.intro: A cool, tropical pudding that is ready when you wake up.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Mango, raspberries and pistachios are featured Ovulatory foods, making a cool, fresh, make-ahead breakfast.
steps: Whisk the chia seeds with the soy milk and maple syrup. Leave for 10 minutes, then whisk again.
Cover and chill for at least 30 minutes, or overnight.
Top with diced mango, raspberries and chopped pistachios.

recipes.title: Peach, Raspberry & Hazelnut Breakfast Quinoa
recipes.intro: A warm, creamy quinoa bowl topped with cool fruit.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Peaches, raspberries and hazelnuts are featured Ovulatory foods, making a bright, light breakfast with quinoa for substance.
steps: Rinse the quinoa and simmer it in the soy milk and about ½ cup (100 ml) water for 18 to 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft and creamy.
Slice the peaches and chop the hazelnuts.
Spoon into bowls and top with the peaches, raspberries, hazelnuts, cinnamon and maple syrup.

recipes.title: Lime-Ginger Tofu & Pineapple Rice Bowl
recipes.intro: Crisp tofu and juicy pineapple over rice, with a zingy lime and ginger finish.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Tofu, pineapple, bean sprouts and red pepper are featured Ovulatory foods, making a crisp, bright, quick-cooked rice bowl.
steps: Cook the rice according to the packet.
Fry the cubed tofu in the oil for 6 minutes until golden, then add the sliced pepper and grated ginger for 3 minutes.
Add the pineapple chunks and bean sprouts and cook for 2 minutes, then season with salt and lime juice.
Serve over the rice.

recipes.title: Banana & Buckwheat Porridge with Soy Milk
recipes.intro: A creamy, dairy-free porridge made with buckwheat groats.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Buckwheat, bananas and walnuts are featured Luteal foods, making a cosy, filling vegan porridge.
steps: Rinse the buckwheat and simmer with the soy milk, about ½ cup (100 ml) water and one mashed banana for 12 to 15 minutes, stirring now and then.
Slice the second banana and chop the walnuts.
Spoon into bowls and top with the banana, walnuts and cinnamon.

recipes.title: Split Pea & Parsnip Soup
recipes.intro: A thick, sweet-savoury soup that is easy to batch-cook and freeze.
recipes.whyThisPhase: Split peas and parsnips are featured Luteal foods, and the split peas bring protein and fibre to a thick, warming soup.
steps: Soften the chopped onion in the oil for 4 minutes, then add the garlic, diced parsnips and thyme for 2 minutes.
Add the rinsed split peas and the stock, bring to the boil and simmer for 35 to 40 minutes, stirring now and then, until the peas collapse.
Blend part of the soup for a thicker texture, season and serve.
